title: Amendment 3 passed. Here is what changes on a Vero Beach homeowner's tax bill, and when.
seoTitle: Amendment 3 Passed: What It Means in Vero Beach
description: Florida voters approved Amendment 3. What the bigger homestead exemption means for Vero Beach homeowners, when it reaches tax bills, and what to do now.
dek: Amendment 3 cleared the 60% bar on Tuesday. The bigger homestead exemption does not touch the tax bill on your counter today. Here is when it does, what it covers, and who won the three Vero Beach City Council seats.
facebook: Amendment 3 passed. So is your Vero Beach tax bill smaller this month? Not yet. Here is when the bigger homestead exemption kicks in, what it does and does not cover, and the simple things to check on your home now.
keywords: Indian River County property tax Amendment 3
Vero Beach City Council election results 2026

body.text: Florida voters said yes to Amendment 3 on Tuesday. It passed with 62% of the vote, two points above the 60% a change to the state constitution needs. If you own and live in a home in Vero Beach or anywhere in Indian River County, this is the measure that raises your homestead exemption.

The big question this morning is simple: does my bill go down now? The short answer is no. The tax bill you got this month is not affected. This article explains when the change shows up, what it covers, and what is still unknown. It also lists who won the three Vero Beach City Council seats.

body.title: The short version
body.text: Amendment 3 takes effect January 1, 2027. WFTV reported the change first shows up on tax bills mailed in November 2027. Your November 2026 bill stays the same, and paying it in November still earns the biggest early-payment discount.
Here is what the amendment does, based on reporting from CBS12, WFTV and WUSF:

items: Homestead owners: the exemption on non-school property taxes goes from $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027, then to $250,000 in 2028. After that it can be adjusted for inflation.
School taxes are not part of the increase. The first $25,000 of today's exemption still applies to all property taxes, including school taxes, WUSF reported.
Rentals, second homes and commercial property: the yearly cap on how fast assessed value can rise for non-school taxes drops from 10% to 5%.
New homeowners: people who start a homestead later get the smaller exemption at first. They qualify for the bigger one in their fifth year of receiving a homestead exemption, WFTV reported.

body.text: It will not make your whole tax bill disappear, CBS12 noted. Your bill has several lines: county, city, school board, hospital district and others. The bigger exemption only lowers the taxable value used for the non-school lines.

Two other amendments failed. Amendment 1, about the state's rainy-day fund, got 40%. Amendment 2, a property tax break for some farm equipment and agricultural property, got about 58%, short of the 60% it needed.
What it means for county services

A bigger exemption means less property tax money coming in to local governments. Before the vote, Indian River County staff estimated the county would collect about $22 million less in the 2027-28 budget year and about $41 million less the year after, Sebastian Daily reported. Those were estimates. No service cuts tied to the amendment had been adopted.

The Florida Trib reported that leaders of the Indian River County hospital district say it could lose about a third of its tax money. Statewide, economists estimate local governments will collect $4.9 billion less in the first year, growing to $11.8 billion by 2031.

The amendment does not automatically require cuts to police or other programs, CBS12 reported. Each city, county and district decides how to respond in its own budget. The Florida Trib reported the Legislature still has to write the rules that put the amendment in place, and those rules are not written yet.
Who won the Vero Beach City Council seats
Vero Beach voters also filled three at-large City Council seats on Tuesday. TCPalm reported these unofficial results:

items: Tracey Zudans, a former council member: 14.2%

body.text: Each seat is a two-year term. The three winners will make up the council majority for the next two years, TCPalm reported. Issues in the race included the Three Corners waterfront project and airport expansion. The council also sets the city's budget and tax rate, which is one of the lines that Amendment 3 touches starting next year.

items: Pay this month's bill as usual. It is not changed by Amendment 3. Paying in November earns the 4% early-payment discount.

Make sure your homestead is on file. Look up your parcel on the Indian River County Property Appraiser's website, ircpa.org, and check which exemptions you have. The bigger exemption is tied to homestead.
Bought your home this year? The deadline to file for homestead for 2027 is March 1, 2027. Remember the new five-year rule for the larger exemption.
Own a rental or second home? The change for you is the 5% cap on assessment increases for non-school taxes, not the homestead exemption.
Watch your TRIM notice next August. That mailer shows your proposed taxes and the dates of the county and city budget hearings, where you can speak.
Check back for final numbers. Tuesday's results are unofficial until they are certified. The Supervisor of Elections posts results at voteindianriver.gov.

body.text: The details of how the new exemption is applied will come from the Legislature and the Property Appraiser in the months ahead. For now, the most useful thing you can do is make sure your homestead paperwork is right.

faq.a: Yes. Amendment 3 passed on November 3, 2026, with about 62% of the vote. It needed 60%.
January 1, 2027. WFTV reported the change first shows up on property tax bills mailed in November 2027. Your November 2026 bill is not affected.

faq.q: How much is the new homestead exemption under Amendment 3?
faq.a: For non-school property taxes, it rises from $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and to $250,000 in 2028, then can be adjusted for inflation. School taxes are not part of the increase.

faq.q: Does Amendment 3 help owners of rentals or second homes?
faq.a: It lowers the yearly cap on assessment increases for non-homestead property from 10% to 5% for non-school taxes. The bigger exemption is only for homestead.

faq.q: Who won the Vero Beach City Council election in 2026?
faq.a: Unofficial results show incumbents Aaron Vos and Linda Moore and former council member Tracey Zudans won the three seats. Each term is two years.
